items.title: Three Mississauga Mayoral Candidates Make Their Case to Students as Parrish Skips UTM Forum
items.summary: The Varsity reports that three Mississauga mayoral candidates addressed students at a University of Toronto Mississauga Students' Union election forum on Oct. 14, ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, Ward 2 Councillor Alvin Tedjo, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, and Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla each took questions separately for about 30 minutes at the event, held at the Blind Duck. The outlet reports incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish declined to attend, and organizers said they had not received a specific explanation beyond her earlier decision to take part in only three debates during the campaign. UTMSU President Adam El-Falou, who moderated the forum, said the union invited the four candidates based on polling and wanted to give students a chance to raise concerns about rising living costs, unreliable transit and limited job opportunities. According to The Varsity, Tedjo used the forum to propose five new Bus Rapid Transit routes along Erin Mills Parkway, Dundas Street West, Lakeshore Road, Derry Road and Dixie Road, saying work could begin in his first term with dedicated lanes and signals to speed up service.

items.title: Brampton Diners Won't Need the Drive to Mississauga Much Longer as Mughal Mahal Plans Expansion
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that Mughal Mahal, a Mississauga restaurant known for its Punjabi cuisine, is opening a second location in Brampton. According to the outlet, the restaurant announced the move on social media with the message "Same flavours. New location." The outlet reports no opening date has been set, though the restaurant says the new spot is coming soon. Insauga.com says the restaurant specializes in Amritsari kulcha, a buttery stuffed flatbread from the Punjabi city of Amritsar that is baked in a tandoor and traditionally served with chole, a spiced chickpea dish. According to the restaurant, the new Brampton location will carry the same menu as the original. The outlet notes Mughal Mahal has been serving Indian food since 1990, according to its website.

items.title: Vandalism, Vote-Day Disputes Overshadow Mississauga's Sign Bylaw Crackdown Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: CityNews reports Mississauga election signs have become a flashpoint in the mayoral race, with the city removing illegally placed signs as candidates report vandalism and disputes over placement. According to the city, crews are proactively patrolling and removing signs that violate the municipal sign bylaw, which bars election signs on public property, anywhere they block visibility, and within 50 metres of a polling station. The outlet reports the city charges a $20-per-day storage fee only if a candidate retrieves an impounded sign, and otherwise disposes of unclaimed signs after 30 days. CityNews reports mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo's campaign says its signs have been stolen, damaged and vandalized throughout the race. Campaign spokesperson Kris Pangilinan said volunteers have reported being followed by supporters of opposing campaigns while canvassing and that paid protesters have shown up at campaign events.

items.title: First International Super Miniso Concept Store Brings Blind-Box Toys and Licensed Characters to Square One
items.summary: InsideHalton.com reports the first international Super Miniso concept store opened at Mississauga's Square One mall on Oct. 10, with a Miniso Land store set to follow in November. According to the outlet, the retailer offers original products with trendy designs, including licensed merchandise from Disney and other popular brands. The outlet reports Miniso was founded a decade ago in Guofu Ye's garage in Guangzhou, China, with a company mission to bring what it calls a relaxed and joyful lifestyle to consumers worldwide. InsideHalton.com says one of the store's most popular draws is the blind box, where shoppers pick a favourite cartoon brand and receive a surprise item inside. The outlet reports the opening has already drawn crowds of excited shoppers to the Mississauga mall.

items.title: Moderate UV and Gusty Winds Accompany Sunday's Mild, Sunny Stretch in Toronto and the GTA
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Toronto and much of the Greater Toronto Area will see sunny skies and relatively mild temperatures on Sunday, Oct. 18, according to Environment Canada. The outlet says Toronto and Mississauga are forecast to reach daytime highs of 16 C, while Halton Region tops out around 15 C and Hamilton also reaches 16 C. Insauga.com reports the sunshine will come with noticeable wind, as southwesterly gusts strengthen through the morning to around 40 km/h in Toronto, Mississauga and Halton. The outlet says Hamilton could see stronger gusts, up to 50 km/h, during the day. Insauga.com notes the UV index is expected to reach a moderate 4, meaning anyone spending extended time outdoors may still want sun protection despite the cooler fall air, with clear conditions expected to hold into Sunday evening and overnight.

items.title: Homes Bear Brunt of Break-Ins as Peel Police Data Shows 41 Incidents Across Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Regional Police's crime occurrence mapping portal recorded 41 break-ins across Mississauga and Brampton between Sept. 17 and Oct. 17. According to the outlet, Brampton accounted for the larger share with 27 reported break-ins, compared with 14 in Mississauga over the same month. The outlet reports clusters emerged in specific corridors, with three incidents in the Dundas Street area of Mississauga and two near Steeles Avenue in Brampton. Insauga.com says homes made up the largest category of targets at 16 incidents, followed by seven restaurants and six stores. The outlet reports police are urging residents and business owners to take precautions to help protect their properties from break-ins.
